system_map.overview: The system is a Continuous Architecture Steering (CAS) runner that processes architectural deltas, enforces governance rules, and generates actions. It is structured as a layered Python application with clear separation between CLI, orchestration, domain models, and infrastructure adapters.

layers.name: application
layers.purpose: Orchestration, flow execution, and service coordination

layers.name: domain
layers.purpose: Domain models and business logic entities

layers.name: infrastructure
layers.purpose: External adapters, bootstrap utilities, and LLM clients

patterns.name: Pydantic Domain Entity Modeling
patterns.summary: Uses Pydantic models to define structured domain entities for governance and steering.
patterns.intent: To provide a type-safe, validated representation of domain concepts.
patterns.context: The system models complex governance concepts like inventories, compliance findings, capabilities, and architectural deltas.
forces: Need for validation and type safety
patterns.solution: Define all domain objects as Pydantic BaseModel subclasses with typed fields and validators.
implementation_signals: Presence of pydantic models across multiple modules
Use of typed hints and nested models

evidence.note: Core governance domain entities modeled with Pydantic
Steering and capability domain entities with validation

benefits: Enables IDE support for type checking
costs: Potential performance overhead in large-scale object creation
failure_modes: Over-reliance on Pydantic features leading to complex validators
Mixing persistence concerns into entity models

patterns.reuse_notes: Apply to any domain with rich structured data. Use inheritance and composition to model hierarchies.

extraction_metadata.method: Inferred from consistent use of Pydantic in multiple model files

patterns.name: Transition Registry State Machine
patterns.summary: A registry that maps allowed state transitions for governance actions.
patterns.intent: To centralize and ensure valid state changes in an action workflow.
patterns.context: GovernanceActionEngine needs to track states of actions and ensure valid transitions.
patterns.solution: Use a TransitionRegistry that defines possible transitions and validates them against a state model.

evidence.note: Central registry for transitions in action engine

benefits: Makes state machine explicit and testable
costs: Additional abstraction layer may be overkill for simple flows
failure_modes: Incomplete transition definitions leading to runtime errors

patterns.reuse_notes: Use when multiple stateful entities require controlled transitions. Ensure transitions are self-documenting.

patterns.name: LLM Client Abstraction (Adapter Pattern)
patterns.summary: Defines a common interface for LLM clients, allowing pluggable backends.
patterns.intent: To decouple core logic from specific LLM providers.
patterns.context: The system needs to use different LLM providers (LiteLLM, mock) without impacting other components.
forces: Minimize impact of provider API changes
patterns.solution: Create a client protocol/interface, with multiple implementations (e.g., LiteLLMClient, MockLLMClient) conforming to the same interface.

benefits: Enables swapping LLM backends without changing core logic
Allows future support for other providers
costs: A small abstraction layer adds indirection
failure_modes: If interface is too generic, losing provider-specific features

patterns.reuse_notes: Define a minimal interface that covers common use cases. Use dependency injection to select implementation.

extraction_metadata.method: Presence of multiple client classes with consistent naming in llm/

patterns.name: Layered Architecture
patterns.summary: Presents a clean separation between CLI, application logic, domain models, and infrastructure.
patterns.context: The project structure shows distinct layers, enabling maintainability.
forces: Testability of domain and application logic
patterns.solution: Organize code into presentation (CLI), application (runner, services), domain (models), and infrastructure (LLM clients, bootstrap).
implementation_signals: Directory structure: cli.py, runner.py, governance/, llm/

costs: Overhead of passing data through layers
failure_modes: Layers becoming too coupled if rules are relaxed

patterns.reuse_notes: Use when project size justifies separation. Ensure dependencies point inward (domain independent).

extraction_metadata.method: Inferred from project structure and file/directory organization

patterns.name: Pure Function for Health Metrics
patterns.summary: Health calculation implemented as a pure function with no side effects.
patterns.context: The dashboard requires health status based on metrics.
patterns.solution: Implement calculate_health as a pure function that takes metrics and returns HealthStatus.

benefits: Can be reused in multiple contexts
failure_modes: If function becomes impure over time (e.g., reads external state)

patterns.reuse_notes: Prefer pure functions for calculations without side effects.

patterns.name: Rule-Based Compliance Engine
patterns.summary: A dedicated engine that evaluates compliance against a set of rules.
patterns.intent: To centralize and manage compliance checking.
patterns.context: The system must validate governance compliance.
patterns.solution: Implement ComplianceEngine that can process rules, likely using a rule representation.

benefits: Can be extended with new rules
costs: Complexity in rule definition and processing
failure_modes: Rules become too intertwined with engine logic

patterns.reuse_notes: Consider separating rule definitions from engine execution for better extensibility.

extraction_metadata.method: Inferred from class name and purpose

patterns.name: Workspace Bootstrap and Initialization
patterns.summary: A dedicated bootstrap process to set up the workspace, including symlinks and configuration merging.
patterns.intent: To ensure consistent initial setup across environments.
patterns.context: The system can be bootstrapped into a project.
patterns.solution: Provide a bootstrap function that initializes workspace, creates symlinks, and merges configuration blocks.
implementation_signals: Use of symlink creation and config merging functions

evidence.note: Setup actions for workspace and configuration

failure_modes: If bootstrap script fails silently, leading to inconsistent state

patterns.reuse_notes: Use for any tool that needs to initialize a workspace within an existing project.

patterns.name: Data Transfer Objects for Ingestion
patterns.summary: Uses DTOs like RawGitDelta and ArchitecturalDelta to structure external data.
patterns.intent: To decouple external input formats from internal processing.
patterns.context: The system receives git changes and transforms them.
forces: Need to adapt to varying input
patterns.solution: Define DTOs for raw data and processed data, allowing transformations in between.
implementation_signals: Class names starting with Raw or representing input structures

evidence.note: DTOs for git changes and architectural deltas

patterns.reuse_notes: Use when transforming external data into domain models.

patterns.name: Action Engine and Service Layer
patterns.summary: Separation between engine (processing logic) and service (orchestration).
patterns.intent: To isolate business rules from external effects.
patterns.context: Governance actions are processed via a service.
patterns.solution: GovernanceActionEngine handles logic, GovernanceActionService orchestrates and integrates with other components.

evidence.note: Engine with core action processing logic

failure_modes: Service becoming a god object if not careful

patterns.reuse_notes: Consider using this pattern when complex actions need both business logic and integration.

extraction_metadata.method: Inferred from separate engine and service classes

patterns.name: Domain Exception Hierarchy
patterns.summary: Defines a custom exception (GovernanceException) for domain-specific errors.
patterns.intent: To distinguish domain errors from generic ones.
patterns.context: The system needs specific error handling for governance issues.
patterns.solution: Create a base domain exception that can be subclassed for specific cases.

evidence.note: Custom exception for governance domain errors

failure_modes: If exception hierarchy becomes too deep

patterns.reuse_notes: Use for errors that need to be distinguished from generic exceptions.
